Subject: Launch week SLA: request for expanded on-call coverage

Marcus —

Our engineering and ops teams just confirmed a hard go-live window for our APAC rollout: 2026-09-28 through 2026-10-02. Given the expected spike in traffic and the regulatory window in our EU customers, we need to request a temporary variance to our support response SLOs for that week. Specifically: 

- P1: 15 minute response target (current contract 5 minutes)
- P2: 60 minute response target (current contract 30 minutes)

We understand this is an exception but it is critical for our phased deployment (canary -> full). Can Redwood provide an operational plan for expanded on-call (additional night responders in APAC and EU overlap) and an escalation path if P1 incidents are not acknowledged?

If you can run this through your ops and legal, procurement wants a one-page amendment they can sign before the 22nd. I've attached our go-live checklist.

Thanks,
Kenji

Kenji —

Thanks for the heads up and congrats on the go-live. We can support a temporary variance but need to lock down the operational commitments and runbook changes before we sign anything. High level plan proposal from our side: 

1) Temporary on-call expansion: add two additional APAC-follow-the-sun responders for 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-02 (hours: 2200-0800 UTC).
2) P1 pledge: we can agree to 15-minute initial response for that week if the expanded rota is staffed and the customer provides a primary P1 contact channel (PagerDuty or direct phone).
3) Escalation path: initial responder -> senior on-call (within 30m) -> infra on-call (within 60m) -> ops director page (within 90m).
4) Post-week RCA and crediting: if we miss P1 pledge more than twice, we will offer a pro-rated credit per existing SLA formula.

I'll put together a one-page variance doc for procurement to sign. Can your security/ciso confirm there's no regulatory blocker to expanding coverage into the EU/JP hours?

I'll loop in AV and Evelyn to confirm staffing.

—Marcus

AV / Marcus / Kenji —

Infra confirmation: we can accept the increased alerting volume for the short window. A couple of technical constraints to note: 

- If traffic patterns exceed 3x baseline sustained for >30m, our automated fallback will route to the next model variant, which can increase latency for complex generations. We'll surface these events as P1s only if they impact request success rates or model availability.
- We will enable temporary prefix caching for heavy traffic endpoints to reduce per-token load. That requires a short config change which we will schedule during the early-morning low-traffic slot on 09-28 (target 03:00 UTC).

Operational ask: provide the PagerDuty integration key or confirm the PD team to add (security approval required). Otherwise we'll use the Redwood-managed bridge with a direct dial-out to your on-call list.

-karthik
